title: Excellent Knives Are Included With Costly Magnetic Stand
text:
Excellent Knives Are Included With Costly Magnetic Stand. The Renaissance-series knives in this expensive MERCER CULINARY M21940 RENAISSANCE BOARD MAGNETIC KNIFE SET (6-Piece, 11 3/8" x 9", Stainless Steel) are of superior quality. However, you’re paying a LOT for the weighty (more than 8 lbs.!) acacia-wood magnetic stand in this knife set (about $222 on Amazon for knives and stand). If it's good knives you want, consider this similar [[ASIN:B00MRU46DS Renaissance Wood and Glass Block Set]] (about $155 on Amazon). The difference in the sets are (1) the knife stands, and (2) a filet knife in the expensive set instead of the utility knife in the cheaper set.

Is the magnetic stand worth the extra cost? I don’t think so. The stand is a counter-space hog that is wider than a knife block. It also requires space above the acacia wood rectangle for removing the knives, because they don’t pull off all that easily when pulled straight forward. (Note that the cheaper set also requires vertical space for knife removal.)

A magnetic stand may be a good storage solution for these Renaissance-series knives, because they should be hand-washed and dried. The manufacturer’s website states: “Cutlery should never be washed in a dishwasher: the intense heat and radical temperature changes may cause the handle to deteriorate; the blade edges will become dull through rubbing against each other; and caustic soap will cause staining and pitting of the blade.”

However, the set does NOT include a sharpening steel (which the magnetic stand probably doesn't support). The set is shipped as (1) an 8-lb. magnetic stand in a box (some assembly required), and (2) five separate knives in retail hanging-display clamshell packaging.

The Renaissance-series knives are Mercer’s most expensive knives for non-professional cooks. They’re comparable to Wusthof Classic knives.
